- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), especially if sentiment is neutral or positive; cap forecast at 5–10% below peak observed.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 85→70, 80→65), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 2–3 periods post-spike.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic when sentiment is high; apply a 1–2% downward correction if sentiment >0.75 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model may misread trend; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to adjust forecast direction.
